options.label: Send a patrol to probe their lines
options.narrative_hint: A cautious skirmish — your scouts test Voss's forces but avoid a decisive engagement. You learn something, but Voss sees hesitation.

options.label: March a garrison force to repel the raiders
options.narrative_hint: A respectable show of force. Your soldiers push back the raiders but take losses. Voss may think twice, or may escalate.

options.label: Commit the full army to crush them decisively
options.narrative_hint: An all-out assault. If successful, Voss's raiding force is shattered and his reputation suffers — but the cost in blood and coin is steep.

options.label: Pull back and cede the border villages
options.narrative_hint: Discretion wins today, but your people see cowardice. The border folk feel abandoned. Voss grows bolder.

options.label: Execute the spy publicly as a warning
options.narrative_hint: A brutal message to Lady Morath: her agents die screaming. Your court is rattled, but fear keeps tongues still. Morath takes it personally.

options.label: Turn the spy into a double agent
options.narrative_hint: A risky gambit. Feed Morath false intelligence through her own operative. If she discovers the ruse, the consequences will be severe.

options.label: Release the spy with a peace overture to Morath
options.narrative_hint: An act of calculated mercy. Morath may see wisdom in negotiation — or she may see weakness ripe for exploitation.

options.label: Accept Ashford's alliance on his terms
options.narrative_hint: Ashford's terms are lopsided but the alliance is genuine. You gain a powerful ally but at an ongoing cost that drains your treasury. Your people wonder who truly rules.

options.label: Counter with your own terms
options.narrative_hint: Bold negotiation. Ashford respects ambition but does not tolerate being dictated to. The talks could stall entirely.

options.label: Reject the alliance in open court
options.narrative_hint: A dramatic refusal that energizes your base but makes a permanent enemy of the realm's most connected lord. Ashford does not forget humiliation.

options.label: Hire the operative and fund a spy network
options.narrative_hint: A shadowy figure known only as Whisper offers their services. Their intelligence is invaluable but their loyalty is to coin, not crown. Your court grows uneasy around this new presence.

options.label: Hire them on a trial basis with limited access
options.narrative_hint: Cautious engagement. Whisper accepts the leash but chafes under restrictions. You get some intelligence but miss the deeper currents.

options.label: Turn them away — spies cannot be trusted
options.narrative_hint: Principled but potentially costly. Your court approves of the moral stand, but in a realm of scheming rivals, blindness has its price. Morath's agents operate unchecked.

options.label: Welcome Sage Corwin to your council
options.narrative_hint: An aging scholar-diplomat offers to serve your court. His idealism borders on naivety, but his network of contacts across rival courts is unmatched. Your military advisors distrust him.

options.label: Hire him as an envoy, not a full advisor
options.narrative_hint: A limited role. Corwin accepts gracefully but you miss the depth of his counsel. He serves as a messenger rather than a strategist.

options.label: Refuse — diplomats are a luxury you cannot afford
options.narrative_hint: Your war council nods approval but the realm's political isolation deepens. Words, it seems, are weapons your rivals will wield without opposition.

title: A Crown of Thorns and Roses

options.label: Accept the marriage and bind your houses
options.narrative_hint: A political marriage to Lady Morath's kin. The alliance is powerful but the entanglement is permanent. Morath's spies become your household, and your court whispers of puppet rulers.

options.label: Negotiate stricter marriage terms to limit Morath's influence
options.narrative_hint: You try to bind Morath while keeping her at arm's length. The negotiations are tense and may collapse, but if they hold, you gain an ally without losing sovereignty.

options.label: Decline with diplomatic courtesy
options.narrative_hint: A polite refusal that preserves relations but closes a door. Morath accepts the rejection outwardly but privately considers you an obstacle rather than a partner.

options.label: Seize the trade route and impose heavy tolls
options.narrative_hint: Aggressive commerce — you garrison the crossroads and tax every wagon. Gold flows in but merchants reroute and neighboring lords cry foul. Ashford in particular takes notice.

options.label: Negotiate shared control with neighboring lords
options.narrative_hint: Diplomacy at the crossroads. You split the revenue but build goodwill. The arrangement is fragile and requires ongoing maintenance — and stationing guards at the crossing costs soldiers.

options.label: Maintain the route but keep tolls minimal
options.narrative_hint: A light touch that attracts merchants but earns modest revenue. Your people benefit from cheaper goods, but rival merchants exploit the open road to undercut your own traders.

options.label: Blockade the route to starve rival supply lines
options.narrative_hint: A wartime maneuver in peacetime. You hurt your rivals but devastate local commerce. Merchants flee, but Voss and Morath feel the pinch.

options.label: Hire the full company — pay their price
options.narrative_hint: The Iron Wolves are expensive but fearsome. Your army swells dramatically, but mercenary loyalty is bought, not earned. Your regular soldiers resent the newcomers.

options.label: Hire only their scouts and outriders
options.narrative_hint: A selective contract. You gain elite reconnaissance without the full cost or the loyalty problems. But in a pitched battle, scouts alone will not turn the tide.

options.label: Refuse — your army fights for honor, not coin
options.narrative_hint: Principled but militarily costly. Your soldiers respect the decision but the Iron Wolves sell their swords to Lord Voss instead, strengthening his forces.

options.label: Send a small detachment to guard the granaries
options.narrative_hint: A token force protects some grain but the raiders are numerous. You save what you can but the losses sting. People grumble about inadequate protection.

options.label: Deploy a garrison to intercept the raiders
options.narrative_hint: A solid defensive response. Your soldiers engage the raiders and recover most of the stolen grain, though casualties mount and the campaign costs.

options.label: Launch a punitive expedition to destroy the raiders' camp
options.narrative_hint: A devastating counter-strike. You annihilate the raider camp and recover stolen goods, but the campaign strips your army and strains supplies. Rumors suggest the raiders were funded by a rival lord.

options.label: Abandon the outer granaries and consolidate supplies
options.narrative_hint: A painful triage. You save your soldiers but the grain burns. Hunger will follow, and the raiders grow emboldened for next time.

options.label: Launch a quiet investigation before acting
options.narrative_hint: Patience and subtlety. You trace the corruption through your court, uncovering its full extent. But the delay allows the traitor to destroy evidence — or worse, to act first.

options.label: Arrest the suspects immediately
options.narrative_hint: Swift justice — or swift injustice. You round up the suspected traitors and make examples of them. Some are guilty, but innocents may be caught in the net. Fear settles over the court.

options.label: Offer amnesty in exchange for information
options.narrative_hint: Mercy as strategy. The traitor reveals their patron — a rival lord — but your court questions whether betrayal should go unpunished. Trust is cheapened.

options.label: Accept the challenge with a defensive posture
options.narrative_hint: You meet Voss on the field but hold back your reserves. A measured response that limits losses but also limits any chance of a decisive outcome. Voss mocks your caution.

options.label: Match his forces with a balanced army
options.narrative_hint: An even contest of arms. The battle could go either way, and the outcome will reshape the power balance. Win or lose, this fight will be remembered.

options.label: Throw everything into a decisive victory
options.narrative_hint: All or nothing. You commit every soldier, every reserve, every resource to crushing Voss on the field. Victory here could break his power forever — but defeat would leave you defenseless.

options.label: Refuse the challenge and fortify your stronghold
options.narrative_hint: You deny Voss the open battle he craves. Your walls are strong, but your reputation suffers. Voss parades through your lands unopposed, burning villages to draw you out.

options.label: Play the council factions against each other
options.narrative_hint: Machiavellian scheming. You pit Ashford's supporters against Voss's allies and extract concessions from both. Clever, but dangerous — if either side discovers your game, you face unified opposition.

options.label: Build your own voting bloc with gifts and promises
options.narrative_hint: Patronage politics. You buy loyalty with gold and favors, building a coalition of minor lords who owe you everything. Expensive but effective — until the money runs out.

options.label: Denounce the council's corruption publicly
options.narrative_hint: A bold populist move. You call out the rot in the political system, winning the hearts of commoners but alienating the very lords you need to govern. Ashford is furious.

options.label: Abstain and let the council sort itself out
options.narrative_hint: Strategic patience — or fatal indecision. You conserve political capital while others exhaust theirs. But the council's decisions may not favor your interests.
